Gordie Howe, nicknamed Mr. Hockey, is a legendary Canadian right-winger who dominated the sport over a thirty-two season career spanning from nineteen forty-six to nineteen eighty. His combination of scoring ability, physical toughness, and longevity made him the standard by which hockey greatness was measured before Gretzky rewrote the record book.

He scored eight hundred one goals and one thousand forty-nine assists for one thousand eight hundred fifty career points across regular season and playoffs combined, records that stood until Gretzky surpassed them. Howe won the Hart Trophy for MVP six times and played on six Stanley Cup championship teams with the Detroit Red Wings. He played the majority of his career with the Detroit Red Wings from nineteen forty-six to nineteen seventy-one, establishing the franchise's identity during its dominant era.

He was known for a ferocious physical game combined with finesse. His elbows and stick-work were legendary, earning him respect and fear in equal measure. He returned to professional hockey with the Houston Aeros of the WHA at age forty-five, proving his durability and skill. He wore number nine, which became iconic in hockey culture. Throughout his career, he played through a wrist injury for much of the time, demonstrating extraordinary toughness and pain tolerance.
